Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Latin word

petō

petō, petere, petīvī (petiī), petītum

verb, third conjugation, with an accusative

apply for, seek (a post); stand for (office); go for, fetch (a thing)

In this lexicon

  • apply

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. Att. 1.1.2: nēmō est enim ex iīs quī nunc petunt; Liv. 26.18.7: professus sē petere

  • get

    the recommended word · classical · Gell. 17.8.8: nōnne īs curriculō atque oleum petis?; Plin. NH 9.169: petere Brundisium ostreās (Lewis & Short)

Examples

  • nēmō est enim ex iīs quī nunc petunt quī, sī in nostrum annum reciderit, firmior candidātus fore videātur

    For of those now standing there is no one who, if his election falls in my year, would look like a stronger candidate.Cic. Att. 1.1.2

    In the entry for apply

  • quattuor et vīgintī fermē annōs nātus, professus sē petere, in superiōre unde cōnspicī posset locō cōnstitit

    About twenty-four years old, he declared that he was standing, and took his place on higher ground where everyone could see him.Liv. 26.18.7

    In the entry for apply

  • Petīsne illud mūnus?

    Are you applying for that job?composed

    In the entry for apply

  • verberō … nōnne īs curriculō atque oleum petis?

    You rascal … won’t you run and get some oil?Gell. 17.8.8

    I’ll go and fetch the doctor, as fast as I can.Plaut. Men. 875
